edit.description: `harness_relative` (:2182) strips the canonical root as a prefix and, when the target sits above it, falls back to the absolute path (`Err(_) => to_lock_path(&target_abs)`, :2195) — so the committed row spells THIS checkout. Its two callers are the two families whose paths arrive SDK-resolved and absolute: composed-prose includes (:1347) and declared inputs (:2157). Record a `../`-segmented path from the root instead, and refuse loud (a new `DriftError` variant, matched nowhere outside this module) only where no relative path exists — a target on another Windows drive. The read side already works: `resolve_source_dependency` (:2103) joins `harness_root` onto the row and `source_dep_stale_from_doc` (:3406) does the same at check, and a layout region's `import` above the root ALREADY records `../` through that join — the precedent this aligns the two absolute-arriving families with. Rewrite the doc sentence at :2174 that sanctions the absolute fallback ("keeps its absolute form, still readable, just unrooted") — it is the only place the current behavior is stated.

`normalize_path` (:11) already keeps a leading `..` with nothing to pop, which is what makes a `../`-spelled row join back correctly — no change needed there. If the lexical root→target relative derivation is extracted rather than written inline, this module is its home, beside `normalize_path` and `HarnessRelativePath`: path mechanics have one home, and `pathdiff` is outside the sanctioned crate set.

Beside `a_lock_with_composed_prose_includes_emitted_from_a_foreign_cwd_is_harness_relative` (:1680): the same program emitted from two different checkout paths writes a byte-identical lock when its include target sits above the harness root.
The input family's half: a member declaring `input(import.meta.url, "../../src/x.txt")` records `../../src/x.txt`, and the drift read resolves it under a second checkout root.

summary: A source dependency above the harness root records an absolute path in the committed lock, so the lock stops being reproducible across checkouts.

tests.asserts: one program emitted from two checkout paths writes a byte-identical lock when an include target sits above the harness root
an input above the root records a `../`-segmented path and resolves under a second checkout root

acceptance: `cargo test` green with the include and input families both recording a `../`-segmented source path for a target above the harness root, the same lock bytes from two checkout paths, and a loud refusal where no relative path exists.
notes: Consumer report on 0.0.19 (win32), reproduced on linux at 4756671c; re-verified this tick — no commit touched src/ since. Windows also carries canonicalize's `//?/C:/` verbatim prefix, so such a lock is unreadable on linux. No test pins the absolute fallback; only the doc sentence sanctions it. scoped at 3201cbbc

edit.description: `Selection::values` (:706) keeps `value.as_scalar()?` only, so a `FeatureValue::List` contributes nothing to either side of `out_of_set` (:966) — the allowed set and the checked values alike — and the clause decides nothing over a list. The each-grain family has no such hole: `addressed` (:1638) locates one node per `[*]` element, but `addressed_field` (:315) deliberately excludes the set predicates ("read by their own judges over a resolved selection, never parsed as a member-local path"), so `membership("emits[*]", ...)` is unspellable and the bare key is the only spelling there is. Read a list per element on both sides: the allowed set is the union of the satisfiers' values with lists flattened, each element of the member's own value is checked, and each out-of-set element is its own finding naming the member and the element. Leave `duplicates` (:936), `values`' other consumer, reading exactly what it reads today — `unique` over a list is the open `(unique-over-a-list)` fork, so the per-element projection is membership's own or `values` gains an explicit grain its two callers pick.

The membership judge's integration home. A satisfier declaring a scalar and a satisfier declaring a list both contribute to the allowed set; a member whose list carries two out-of-set elements fires two findings, each naming its element; a member whose list is wholly drawn from the set passes; the scalar case stays byte-identical.

summary: A `membership` clause over a list-valued field checks nothing and exits 0 — a list contributes no value to the allowed set or to the checked values.

tests.asserts: a list-valued field is judged per element on both sides — each out-of-set element is its own finding, a fully drawn list passes, and the scalar reading is unchanged

acceptance: `cargo test` green with `membership` firing one finding per out-of-set element of a list-valued field, satisfiers' lists flattened into the allowed set, and the `unique` judge's behavior unchanged.
notes: Consumer report on 0.0.18 and 0.0.19, reproduced at 4756671c; re-verified this tick — no commit touched src/ since. Invariant 6 forbids the silent pass; contract.md "clause" puts membership at the whole grain and is silent on containers, which is why only the per-element reading of a plural feature is derived here. The `unique` half rides its fork. scoped at 3201cbbc

edit.description: Two halves of one enumeration, re-cited against the module 842884f4 rewrote. (1) `discover` (:432) collects *files* per kind, so a `.claude/settings.json` carrying no hooks at all still reports `hook 1` — a file count printed under `render_discovery`'s (:451) "members by kind" heading; a registration kind's members are the entries at its `collection_address`, so the count comes from reading them. (2) `scaffold` (:1741) skips (:1755) reads `kind.content != kind::Content::File` under a comment naming only layout kinds, so every fields-shape kind — `hook`, `installed-plugin`, `known-marketplace`, `mcp-server` — is dropped silently and the container's first emit sheds its groups. Convert each discovered collection entry into a member module named by its registration key, so 0016's whole conversion covers a manifest's registration segments and not just the container member the sibling entry lifts. temper's own three gate hooks already reach the program as `hook` modules minted from `GATE_HOOKS` (:204, shipped 842884f4) and are deliberately uncounted by the lift — this entry converts the project's own groups beside them, so the two writers must not collide on `.temper/hooks/<Event>.ts`.

The lift suite: a project whose `.claude/settings.json` carries a `SessionStart` hook group and an `enabledPlugins` entry lifts one module per registration member, the first emit re-renders both segments beside the container's own keys, and the reported discovery count is the registration-entry count — pinned by a second fixture whose settings.json carries no registration segment at all and must report zero for those kinds. A third pin: a project whose own `SessionStart` group is not temper's gate command still lifts as its own module and does not overwrite the `GATE_HOOKS` module at that event.

summary: A registration member reaches no module: a settings.json hook group is counted in discovery and dropped by the lift, so the container's first emit sheds it.

tests.asserts: a settings.json carrying a hook group and an enabledPlugins entry lifts a module per registration member and the first emit re-renders both segments with the container's keys; a settings.json with no registration segment reports zero for those kinds

acceptance: `cargo test` green with `install` over a project whose settings.json carries registration segments producing a module per registration member, the adoption emit re-rendering the file with every segment intact, and the discovery report counting registration entries rather than the manifest file.
notes: Re-measured at e0d0123b: the count is a file count — a settings.json with no hooks, no enabledPlugins and no extraKnownMarketplaces still reports `hook 1`, `installed-plugin 1`, `known-marketplace 1`, one per kind whose locus is that file. Both halves re-verified past 81ee251b, which moved one doc line in the module and neither `discover` nor the content skip. Rests on `(hook-member-identity)`: a lifted hook needs a name, and two groups on one event share one address today. scoped at dfa667d7
